history.period: 10th-11th century CE (per one source, possibly during Vikramaditya V, c. 1014 - verify); inscriptions dating to 1086 AD reported (verify)
history.summary: Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy Temple at Nandikandi (also spelled Nandi Kandi), Sadasivpet mandal, Sangareddy district, is an 11th-century Kalyani Chalukya star-shaped Shiva temple (CSV town and district correct). It is celebrated for its stellate (star-shaped) sanctum with a Bhumija-style shikhara and a navaranga whose four exquisitely sculptured central pillars were each carved from a single stone block - depicting Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Narasimha, Varaha, Nataraja, Mahishasuramardini, Saraswati, Gaja Lakshmi, plus Dikpalakas, Apsaras, Rakshasas, Matrumurtis and Darpan Warriors. Highlights: a huge ornamental black-stone Nandi, a spatika (crystal) linga beside the main lingam, and a toranam entrance with seven inverted lotus petals - said to let the sunrise fall directly on the lingam through the petal-holes at Makara Sankranti (per social-media sources - verify). One source calls it an ASI protected monument (verify). Folklore says Aurangazeb's soldiers came to destroy the temple and fled after a blow to the Nandi's leg produced a huge sound. COORDINATE FLAG: map.geocode matched only Nandikandi village (district level) at low relevance; coordinates are village-level approximate, not the temple itself. Research sources agree on location: less than 1 km from NH-65, about 15 km from Sangareddy.
